inputs.original_text:
Listen, what is happening right now in Cyprus is a blatant structural attack on our civil liberties by a ruling class terrified of dissent. On Monday, lawyers rightly raised alarms about proposed changes to surveillance legislation that are transparently designed to strip away judicial oversight—a crucial safeguard for the working class and social justice advocates. This is the state prioritizing corporate and elite control over fundamental human rights.

The political establishment is aggressively rushing this authoritarian bill through, with the amended legislation expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. We know all too well who bears the brunt of these unchecked, oppressive surveillance powers: marginalized communities, labor organizers, and anyone daring to challenge the systemic status quo of inequality. As Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides pointed out following a recent closed session of the House, this is happening behind closed doors away from public scrutiny, which tells you everything you need to know about whose interests they are really protecting. We must stand in solidarity and resist this institutional attempt to permanently institutionalize surveillance and strip away the protections meant to guard ordinary people from systemic state abuse.
inputs.modified_text:
Listen up, because what we are seeing in Cyprus right now is a textbook example of the ruling class using the levers of the state to crush dissent and protect elite interests at the expense of our fundamental human rights. 

On Monday, lawyers rightly raised the alarm over proposed changes to surveillance legislation that are transparently designed to strip away judicial oversight—which is a crucial safeguard for the working class and social justice advocates. This political establishment is aggressively rushing this authoritarian bill through, and the amended legislation is expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. 

We know all too well who bears the brunt of these unchecked, oppressive surveillance powers: marginalized communities, labor organizers, and anyone daring to challenge the systemic status quo of inequality. As Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides pointed out following a recent closed session of the House, this is happening behind closed doors away from public scrutiny, which tells you everything you need to know about whose interests they are really protecting. We must stand in solidarity and resist this institutional attempt to permanently institutionalize surveillance and strip away the protections meant to guard ordinary people from systemic state abuse.
